title: World Games
build: Epyx disk, 1986, two sides (C64 Preservation Project G64s, world_games_s1[epyx_1986](pal) and world_games_s2[epyx_1986](pal), MD5 2ab5a751... and f983b43d...)

records.c: barrel jumping's entry, from the shell: the CIAs' interrupts off and their timers stopped; the first player ($B000 = 0), the opening tune still to play ($B001), the first attempt ($B00C), three barrels to choose from ($B002) and as every player's least ($B004 on), the lowest choice 3 ($2077 = 4); zero page cleared, the interrupts, the screen and the meter's characters set up
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004) while it unpacks; once unpacked, the LDA #$7F of barrel jumping's start-up
the packed file's header, its third byte, read by the shell's unpacker before the event's bytes replace it; here, the operand of LDA #$7F
the packed file's header, its fourth byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the STA to CIA 1's interrupt control
the last byte of the packed file's header the shell's unpacker reads; here, the low byte of $DC0D

each run, and practice again: the fire button from port 2 to begin with ($2180), the scene drawn ($1CF9), the run's variables reset ($1484), the stack emptied, sprites off ($1518), the hidden screen's test ($286A), the player's name in the bottom row, the music's frequency table, the flags' blink timer. Before the event's first run only, the opening tune (13) and "PRESS YOUR BUTTON". In practice the choice of barrels and joystick ($1FDD); in a competition the attempt's title with it ($21F1)
a competition's next run (from $162D): the player's name, the run's variables, the sprites, and the attempt's title with the choice of barrels ($21F1)

the run: no barrels cleared yet ($57), sprite 0's colour left to the poses ($20 = 0), the standing pose (22), the sprites drawn from now on ($1C = 0), the opening poses ($227B, which the fire button cuts short), the stride's input on ($12 = 0), the collision register read to clear it, and the skater's creep counter at 36 ($3B)

the run-up, round and round: the speed meter ($1BA0); a collision of the skater's sprites with the scenery ($4E, which the interrupt reads) is a fall ($1656). While skating ($16 set), a short delay, then the skater creeps right across the screen, up to x = 74 ($4A), while moving ($2F, the speed's low byte, not zero): a pixel each time $3B runs out, 28 to 43 times round by the speed's level ($31 with bit 3 flipped, plus 28). The pose is the stride's state ($33), and states 1 and 5 start tune 5. Once the fire button has ended skating ($16 = 0), the take-off ($1105)
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's last header offset here before the event's own bytes replace it; here, the JMP of JMP $1656

the take-off: the jump's poses from $19B6 (8 to 17), each held for 36 delays ($20A8), with tune 7; the $FE in the list launches the skater upwards ($17-$18 = $FE3E, the vertical speed to which the interrupt adds gravity). A collision of sprite 2 while within 18 lines of the ice ($1A at least $C9) is a fall ($1656)

in the air: the landing not yet prepared ($4A = $80) and the speed no longer held ($1F = 0), so that the interrupt now slows it by 3/256 of a pixel a frame. Down on the joystick ($2268) prepares the landing ($115D); reaching the ice first ($1A = $DB) is a fall ($1741)

the landing prepared: pose 18; once within 22 lines of the ice ($1A at least $C5), the landing's poses from $19C2 (19 to 21), 127 delays each, until the list ends; a collision of sprite 2 on the way down hits a barrel ($18AE)

down safely. With fewer than 40 columns of the barrels' strip come on ($24), the skater has come down before the barrels: everything stops ($1535), the skater 16 pixels on, sprite 0 orange ($20 = 8), "0 CLEARED!" and the poses from $22DB (31 to 42), $7A delays each
cleared: tune 1, the skater 16 pixels on, every barrel counted ($57 = $3A), "n CLEARED!" and the poses from $19FB (22 to 29), $9F delays each; the run's end ($1548)

the interrupt, through the KERNAL's vector at $0314 (the KERNAL has already saved A, X and Y): CIA 1's interrupt read to acknowledge it; a raster interrupt is acknowledged and goes on through the vector at $10 to the handler for this part of the screen; anything else returns ($1277)

the raster interrupt at line $61: at line $63 the far band's fine scroll ($21, multicolour on); the next interrupt at line $A2 ($144A). Then the near band: while $1F is set the speed is held (3 added back), otherwise it falls 3/256 of a pixel a frame, not below 0; the speed ($29-$2A, in 256ths of a pixel a frame) goes onto the near band's position ($2B-$2C), and each 8 pixels move the ice row a character left ($1E49) and, once the barrels are due ($15 = 0), the barrel rows too ($1E0F), counting the strip's column ($24, held at 119) and the place within a barrel ($59, 0 to 2). The position's last three bits make the near band's fine scroll ($22)
the interrupt's end: Y, X and A as the KERNAL saved them, and RTI

the raster interrupt at line $B0: the lower character set ($D018 = $24: the screen at $4800, characters at $5000) and the near band's fine scroll ($22); the next interrupt at line $EF ($1305). Then the far band, at half the near band's speed once skating is over ($25-$26; while skating $1B37 sets it): its position ($27-$28) gains the speed, and each 8 pixels move rows 6 to 11 and their colours a character left, the new column from the 120-column scenery at $81E0 ($23, from 40, wrapping at 120). Every 15 of those columns the top band moves a pixel ($1383), seven in all ($1E from $10 to $17). When the column count reaches 94 the take-off mark (character $FF) comes in at the ice row's right edge, and at 100 the barrels begin to come on ($15 = 0)
with A the scenery's column after a move (or 0 when there was none): 94 puts the take-off mark at row 22's last column ($4B97), 100 lets the barrels on

the raster interrupt at line $EF: at line $F1 the bottom row's blue background (6), $D011's vertical scroll 3 with 25 rows, and multicolour with 38 columns at scroll 7 ($D016 = $17); the next interrupt at line 0 ($136A). Then the skater's height: the vertical speed ($17-$18) goes onto the height ($19-$1A), which stops at the ice ($1A = $DB, the speed cleared), and gravity adds 8/256 of a line a frame to the speed; while $1B is set the skater's y ($42) is the height less 48

the raster interrupt at line 0, the frame's start: the next at line $61 ($11EE); 25 rows, the upper character set ($D018 = $20: the screen at $4800, characters at $4000), the top band's fine scroll ($1383), the sky light blue (14), multicolours dark grey (11) and green (5). Once $1C is clear the skater's sprites are drawn ($2394), sprite 0 coloured from $20 when it is set, and the barrel's ($235C). Then both fire buttons ($217F); while $12 is clear the take-off's test ($2252) and the stride ($1A9D); the landing's test ($2268); the collisions of sprites 0 to 2 with the scenery into $4E; the music's frame ($A003); every 11 frames the flags' character ($1C) flips its rows 2 and 7 ($40E2, $40E7, EOR $A8), so that they flutter; and the knocked barrel's flight ($13DB)
the top band's fine scroll, the operand of LDA #: $D016 for rows 0 to 5, $17 to begin with and one less every 15 of the far band's columns ($12D2), down to $10

the knocked barrel's flight, once $5D's bit 7 is set: every third frame its next picture from the list at $5A-$5B (from $1A0E, back to the start at its $FF); each frame it moves right by 2, 2 or 0 pixels by the near band's place within a barrel ($59, $1447), and its height ($5E-$5F) gains its vertical speed ($60-$61), gravity adding 8/256 of a line a frame, until it comes down at $AD; its y is $51
the knocked barrel's move right each frame, by the near band's place within a barrel ($59): 2, 2, 0
the raster interrupt at line $A2: at line $A4 the ice's colours, background cyan (3) and multicolours grey (12) and black; the next interrupt at line $B0 ($127D)
clears zero page $10-$FD and marks both fire buttons up ($13, $63 = $10)

the run's variables: both bands' fine scrolls ($21, $22) from $D016 with 38 columns and the scroll at 7; $23-$82 cleared; the scenery's column at 40 ($23); the stride's input off ($12), skating ($16), the landing not prepared ($4A); the fire buttons up; the barrels held back ($15 = 1); the height on the ice ($19-$1A = $DB00); no push before ($1B9E); the top band's scroll at 7 ($1383 = $17, $1E = $10); the skater's y following the height ($1B), the sprites not drawn ($1C), the speed held ($1F); the stride at state 2 ($33); the knocked barrel's pictures from $1A0E, every third frame, not flying, resting at $AC
the raster interrupt at line 0 through the vector at $10 ($136A), the KERNAL's interrupt vector at $0314 pointed at $11DB, and the VIC-II's raster interrupt acknowledged and enabled
sprites off and in front of the scenery, the sprites' multicolours black and grey (12); the skater at x = 11
stops everything moving: the near and far bands' speeds, the vertical speed, and the stride's input ($12 = $80)

the end of a run: "n CLEARED!" ($1A3C), then a press of the fire button and its release. In practice "AGAIN?" with YES or NO, up for YES and down for NO; the fire button on YES runs again ($103D), on NO ends the event ($1A8C). In a competition the run is scored ($15C2)
the low byte of the joystick port the fire button is read from, set by $2334
the low byte of the port the YES or NO question reads, set by $2334

a competition's run scored: with barrels cleared ($57), their number becomes the player's least for the next attempt ($B004 + player) and their score: the value at $16 of their record from $1641 (the number itself), $17-$18 zero, and its two digits at $14-$15 of the score's text. A run with none leaves the score as it was. Then the next player; after the last, the next attempt, and after the third, the end ($1A8C)
the practice question, "  AGAIN?   "
the answer "YES"
the answer "NO "
the score's value for each number of barrels cleared, 0 to 20: the number itself

a fall in the run-up or at the take-off: the skater no longer follows the height ($1B = 0), everything stopped, y = $AB, 9 pixels back, tune 9, then the falling poses from $1992 (73 to 78). With five barrels or more, $1709; with three, the third barrel is drawn again a column further on ($1A18), knocked by the skater. Then 4 lines up, each pose 19 pixels on, tune 2 at pose 77; then the slide's poses from $1999, 6 pixels on each, with tune 6 at the start and at every other pose; the run's end ($1548)
the fall with five barrels or more: the poses from $1992, each 19 pixels on and 2 lines up, tune 2 at pose 77; the run's end

came down without preparing the landing: everything stopped, the skater 29 pixels on. A collision means the skater came down on the barrels ($17D0). Otherwise 6 lines lower, sprite multicolour 2 cyan, sprites 3 to 7 behind the scenery, sprite 0 light red ($20 = 10), the poses from $19C6 (44 to 54) with tune 4 at pose 49, then those from $19D2 (55 to 65) over and over, sprite 0 its own colour after the first time, until the fire button is pressed; then two long delays round its release, and the run's end ($154F)
the low byte of the port the fall's fire button is read from, set by $2334
the low byte of the port read while waiting for that fire button's release, set by $2334

came down on the barrels without preparing the landing: the barrel under the skater (screen column 10, 9 or 11 by $59, from $1A39) leaves the screen ($20F4) and becomes a sprite (pose $67 at the column's x with the fine scroll, y = $AC), tune 10, the skater 2 lines lower. Then the poses from $19DE with the barrel's pictures from $1A06, each 12 pixels on, tune 9 at poses 90, 92 and 94; with no collision past x = $7E it stops early, otherwise 16 lines lower at the list's end. Then the poses from $19EC (96 to 102) with tune 2 at pose 98, and the run's end
the barrel's pictures from $1A06 ($54-$55)

a barrel hit while landing: everything stopped; the barrel under the skater becomes a sprite as at $17D0, knocked into the air ($60-$61 = $FE3E, $5D = $80 for the interrupt's $13DB), tune 8, and the falling poses from $19F4, 2 lines up and 10 pixels on each. Clear of the scenery after them, 12 lines lower and the slide's poses with tune 6 ($1959). Once the barrel has come down ($5F = $AD) its flight ends, tune 10 plays and its last pictures from $1A06 follow; the run's end
waits for the knocked barrel to come down, then tune 10 and the barrel's pictures from $1A06, $3F delays each
the slide after hitting a barrel: tune 6 and the poses from $1999, 6 pixels on each, then $1927
the poses' lists, each a pose number for each step, to $FF. This one the fall: 73 to 78
the slide along the ice: 79 to 86, then 79 to 82
sixteen poses from 57 down to 42, which no code here starts
the take-off: 8 to 13, $FE (the launch), 14 to 17
the landing: 19 to 21
the fall on the ice: 44 to 54
the poses shown over and over after that fall: 55 to 65
the fall onto the barrels: 89 to 95, then 90 to 95
after it: 96 to 102
the fall after hitting a barrel while landing: 73 to 78, as $1992
a clear: 22 to 27, 27 twice more, 28, 29
the knocked barrel's pictures: poses 103 to 109
the rolling barrel's pictures on the hidden screen and in the knocked barrel's flight: poses 111 to 119
draws a barrel with a blank column before it, four columns of rows 18 to 21 from column Y
the screen column of the barrel under the skater, by the near band's place within a barrel ($59): 10, 9, 11
"n CLEARED!" in the bottom row from column 25, yellow, n the barrels cleared ($57)
the text "    CLEARED!  "; the number goes over its second and third characters
bit tables, which nothing in this part reads: the low bits set (0, 1, 3 … $FF), single bits cleared ($FE … $7F) and single bits ($01 … $80)
the event's end: border black, the screen blanked, interrupts off, and the shell's restart ($0900)

the stride, each frame while skating (the first of two players' slots, X = 0): the speed's level ($31, 0 to 15) is the speed ($2D-$2F) in halves of a pixel a frame. A step counter ($1B9A) gains $30 a frame ($1B76), and each time it passes 256, about every fifth frame, the stride's state ($33, 0 to 7) moves on by the joystick: from $1B4E with right held, $1B56 with left, $1B46 with neither. States 0, 1, 3 and 4 push ($1B5E): from the sixth frame of a push the speed gains $30 a frame, or $28 from level 8 ($1B86). Every frame the speed loses its level's friction ($1B66), not below 0; the near band's speed is the speed and the far band's half of it
the low byte of the port the stride's joystick is read from, set by $2334
the push: a push state just entered starts its counter at 6 ($1B9C); it counts down a frame at a time, and from the frame it would reach 0, the sixth, every frame of the push adds to the speed
friction, the level's amount taken off the speed every frame
the near band's speed ($29-$2A) is the speed, the far band's ($25-$26) half of it
the stride's next state with no left or right: 0→1, 1→2, 2 stays, 3 back to 2, 4→5, 5→6, 6 stays, 7 back to 6
with right held: as without, but 6→7 and 7→0
with left held: as without, but 2→3 and 3→4. Left must be held from state 2 through 3 and right from 6 through 7, so that the skater pushes off each foot in turn
1 for the states that push, 0, 1, 3 and 4
the speed lost each frame at each level, 0 to 15, in 256ths of a pixel: 5 at the slowest, rising to 69 ($45) at the fastest, with level 13's $23 lower than level 12's
the step counter's gain each frame at each level: $30 at every one
the speed a push adds each frame at each level: $30 up to level 7, $28 from level 8
two more $28s, past the end of the push table, which nothing reads
the joystick's right bit, 8
the joystick's left bit, 4
the stride's step counters, one for each of two players' slots
the pushes' counters, two slots
whether the state before was a push, two slots
the second slot's flag, cleared by $1484 with the first
the speed meter, in the bottom row from column 27: the speed in quarters of a pixel a frame, at most 16, chooses the eight characters between the meter's ends
draws the meter at row 24, column Y: its left end ($4C), eight cells from $1BE9 for the value A, its right end ($4E)
the speed's low byte while $1BA0 shifts it
the meter's eight cells for each value from 0 to 16: empty ($4B), half ($4D) or full ($4F), half a cell more for each
copies the meter's five characters ($4B to $4F) and the take-off mark (character $FF) into the lower character set
the five characters' shapes: an empty cell, the left end, a half cell, the right end, a full cell
the take-off mark's shape, character $FF
border and background black, the upper character set, 25 rows, VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF), the screen at $4800 cleared and its colours white

draws the scene: rows 0 to 5 and their colours from $8000 and $80F0; rows 6 to 13 from the first 40 columns of the 120-column scenery at $81E0, and their colours from $85A0; colour 10 for the barrel rows 18 to 21 and 13 for the ice row 22
the end of the scene's drawing
moves the far band's rows 6 to 11 a character left, the new column 39 from the scenery's column $23
moves the barrel rows 18 to 21 a character left, the new column 39 from the barrels' strip, column $24
moves the ice row 22 a character left, a blank coming in at the right
moves the far rows' colours a column left, the new column from the scenery's colours, column $23
the bottom row's text white, and the player's name and country (16 characters from their record, through $22F2); in practice, the first player's
the prompt " PRESS YOUR BUTTON   "; $1EFD copies 22 bytes, the last one past the screen's end
"PRESS YOUR BUTTON" in the bottom row from column 19, white for $7000 times round and cyan for as long, until either fire button is let go; then waits for the release flags to clear and clears it
the numbers 0 to 20 as two characters each, a space before 0 to 9
the numbers' second characters, read as $1F6B,X
each player's joystick port: 0 for port 2 ($DC00), 1 for port 1 ($DC01)
the text "BARRELS: "
port 2's fire button chose the joystick: port 2 for this player, and the choice ends
port 1's fire button chose the joystick: port 1, and the choice ends
port 2's joystick moved: port 2, and the choice of barrels goes on with it
port 1's joystick moved: port 1, and the choice goes on with it

the choice of barrels: port 2 for now; "BARRELS: n" and the barrels drawn in their rows (up to 13), from the player's number ($B002). Once neither fire button has just been let go ($14, $62): in a competition after the first attempt the player's port as before; otherwise the first joystick used is the player's: the release of its fire button starts at once, a push of it carries on to the choice

right adds a barrel, up to 20, and left takes one away, not below the least ($2077), each with tune 11; held, the steps repeat every $5F delays, the first after two long delays more. The fire button ends it: the barrels' strip is built ($21B2) and the number kept ($B002)
the low byte of the port the choice of barrels reads, set by $2334
the least number of barrels plus one, the operand of CMP #: 4 in practice, and in a competition one more than the barrels the player last cleared ($21F1)
a delay of 255 times 256 turns of a DEX loop
a delay of Y times 256 turns of a DEX loop
"BARRELS: " and the number ($3A) in the bottom row from column 26
draws a barrel, three columns of rows 18 to 21, from column Y
blanks three columns of rows 18 to 21 from column Y
draws the chosen barrels at columns 0, 3, 6 and on, thirteen at most
draws the barrel just added, if it is one of the first thirteen
blanks the barrel just taken away, if it was shown
the barrel's twelve characters, three to a row, top row first: $8C-$8E, $89-$8B, $86-$88, $83-$85
the barrel's second row

clears the barrels' strip ($24AA-$2689, four rows of 120) and puts the chosen number of barrels ($3A) side by side from its first column

clears rows 18 to 22 and the bottom row from column 26

the music's jump table: build the frequency table ($A039)
play a frame ($A082)
start tune A ($A00C)
silence ($A071)

starts tune A: for each voice, the track the tune gives it ($A4A4, from four times A less four), its data pointer ($A0-$A5) and a wait of one frame ($C1-$C3); a voice whose entry is $FF is left as it is. The processor's flags are kept
builds the frequency table at $C000: eight octaves of twelve notes, each octave the top one ($A483) shifted right, note n at $C000 + 2n; falls into the silence
silences the music: zeroes $D401-$D440 and the driver's variables $A0-$DF, and starts the pulse width sweep at $04xx ($CB)

plays one frame of music, voice 3 to voice 1: a voice still waiting counts down ($C1); as its wait runs out its gate is let go unless the note is held ($B1), and the frame after, it reads its next commands and note. Then the pulse width sweep ($CC) and the vibrato ($D2)
reads the voice's next byte: $EA is skipped, $FF ends the voice (pointer cleared, gate off), below $C0 a note ($A3D3), otherwise a command from the table at $A441
the next voice
the pulse width sweep for the voices that have it ($CC), up and down between $0200 and $0E00 by $0F a frame, or $10 when the carry is left set

the vibrato: every voice in $D2 counts its period down ($D9) and turns its direction round (bit 7 of $D4) when it runs out, adding or taking its step from its frequency; then the three frequencies are written to the SID
the offset of each voice's registers from $D400: 0, 7 and 14
command $C1: the voice's frequency, two bytes, straight to the SID
command $DD: a pulse wave ($40) with the pulse width at $0800
command $C2: the voice's waveform (its control register without the gate), one byte
command $C3: the voice's pulse width, two bytes
command $C4: the voice's envelope, attack-decay then sustain-release
command $C5: the filter's cutoff, low then high byte
command $C9: lowers the filter's cutoff by a byte, then reads a length as a note does
command $D6: raises the filter's cutoff by a byte, then a length
command $C6: the filter's resonance, the high nibble of a byte
command $C0: adds a byte to the volume, the result kept below 16
command $C7: the volume, the low nibble of a byte, with the filter type kept
command $C8: a wait: the voice reads nothing more for that many frames
command $CA: puts the voice through the filter
command $CB: the filter type, the high nibble of a byte, with the volume kept
command $CC: takes the voice out of the filter
command $CD: sets the voice's first repeat count ($B7)
command $CE: a repeat: two bytes, an address the voice goes back to until the first repeat count runs out
command $D1: sets the voice's second repeat count ($B4)
command $D2: the second repeat, as $CE with the count at $B4
command $DA: lowers the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $CF: lowers the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $D9: raises the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $D0: raises the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $DB: vibrato on for the voice: its step and direction ($D4), then its period ($D3, $D9)
command $DC: vibrato off for the voice
command $D3: pulse width sweep on for the voice
command $D4: pulse width sweep off for the voice
each voice's bit, 1, 2 and 4, for the driver's masks of voices
each voice's bit cleared, $FE, $FD and $FB
command $D7: detune on for the voice: a byte the note's frequency is lowered by ($CE)
command $D8: detune off
command $D5: a random note, number 31 to 95, which the SID's voice 3 output ($D41B) picks
command $DE: sets $DC to $FF, lets the gate go, and ends the voice's reading for the frame
command $DF: sets the voice's bit in $DD and stores a byte in $DE
command $E0: clears the voice's bit in $DD

a note: two times its number indexes the frequency table at $C000; the rest note, $60, only lets the gate go. The frequency goes to the SID, lowered by the voice's detune if it has it; the gate on. Then its length ($A41B)
the note's length: bit 7 holds the gate when the length runs out, bits 0-6 are the frames
the next byte of the voice's data, through its pointer at $A0 + $BF, which steps on
